source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which lab pattern fits Addison's disease?
options: Low sodium, high potassium, low glucose
questions.rationale: Low aldosterone and cortisol cause hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, hypoglycemia and hypotension.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Addison's disease (PDF p. 302)
questions.quote: Hyperkalemia, due to decreased secretion of aldosterone.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Bronze skin pigmentation in Addison's disease is due to increased:
questions.rationale: Low cortisol triggers more pituitary ACTH and MSH, causing hyperpigmentation.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Addison's disease (PDF p. 302)
questions.quote: The anterior pituitary gland increases secretion of its hormones, which includes MSH. This causes hyperpigmentation.

questions.subject: NP IV
options: With meals or milk in the morning
On an empty stomach at night
questions.rationale: Food reduces gastric irritation; morning dosing mimics the natural cortisol rhythm.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Steroid therapy (PDF p. 303)
questions.quote: Administer steroids after meals or with milk.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Why must long-term prednisone be tapered rather than stopped abruptly?
questions.rationale: Long-term steroids suppress the adrenals; abrupt withdrawal can cause Addisonian crisis.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Steroid therapy (PDF p. 303)
questions.quote: Dose should be tapered and not stopped abruptly. To prevent Addisonian crisis

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client on long-term steroids should have which lab monitored regularly?
questions.rationale: Steroids cause hyperglycemia, hypokalemia, fluid retention and bone loss.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Steroid therapy (PDF p. 303)
questions.quote: Monitor urine and blood glucose levels and urine ketones.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which diet suits a client on long-term corticosteroids?
questions.rationale: High protein prevents muscle wasting, high potassium prevents hypokalemia, low sodium limits fluid retention.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Steroid therapy (PDF p. 303)
questions.quote: Diet of the client should be high protein, high carbohydrate, high potassium and low sodium diet.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with Addison's disease develops severe hypotension, abdominal pain and confusion after an infection. The priority drug is:
questions.rationale: Addisonian crisis requires IV glucocorticoid (hydrocortisone) and fluids.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Addisonian crisis (PDF p. 304)
questions.quote: Administer glucocorticoid/IV Solu cortef Olydrocortisone sodium succinate), then orally'.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Moon face, buffalo hump, purple striae and thin arms suggest:
questions.rationale: Excess cortisol causes truncal obesity, moon face, buffalo hump, striae, bruising and hyperglycemia.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Cushing's syndrome (PDF p. 304)
questions.quote: Obese trunk, thin arms and legs.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with Cushing's syndrome is at increased risk for:
questions.rationale: Cortisol excess suppresses immunity and causes osteoporosis; protect from infection and trauma.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Cushing's syndrome (PDF p. 305)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Hypertension with low potassium and polyuria suggests:
questions.rationale: Conn's syndrome (aldosterone excess) causes hypertension, hypokalemia, weakness and polyuria; treat with spironolactone.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Hyperaldosteronism (PDF p. 306)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After bilateral adrenalectomy, the client will need:
questions.rationale: Bilateral removal needs lifelong replacement; unilateral needs temporary replacement up to 2 years.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Adrenalectomy (PDF p. 306)
questions.quote: Lifelong glucorticoid replacement is necessary with a bilateral adrenalectomy.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Right after adrenalectomy, the nurse watches closely for:
questions.rationale: Falling catecholamines can cause cardiovascular collapse; the adrenals are vascular, so bleeding is also a risk.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Adrenalectomy (PDF p. 306)
questions.quote: Catecholamine levels drop as a result of surgery, which can result in cardiovascular collapse, hypotension and shock.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Episodes of severe hypertension, headache, sweating and palpitations suggest:
questions.rationale: Pheochromocytoma releases catecholamines: hypertension, headache, hyperhidrosis, hypermetabolism, hyperglycemia.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Pheochromocytoma (PDF p. 307)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with pheochromocytoma should avoid:
questions.rationale: Smoking, caffeine and sudden movement can trigger catecholamine surges and hypertensive crisis.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Pheochromocytoma (PDF p. 307)
questions.quote: Instruct client to avoid smoking, drinking caffeine — containing beverages, or changing position suddenly.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client using intranasal desmopressin should report:
questions.rationale: Too much ADH causes water intoxication: drowsiness, listlessness, headache, shortness of breath.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Antidiuretic hormones (PDF p. 309)
questions.quote: To report signs of water intoxication (drowsiness, listlessness. shortness of breath and headache.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Oral calcium supplements can reduce the absorption of which antibiotic?
questions.rationale: Calcium binds tetracycline and lowers its absorption; separate doses.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 9 Parathyroid medications (PDF p. 311)
questions.quote: Oral calcium salts reduce the absorption of tetracycline HCl.
